key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 boiler steel during cyclic testing at 900°C.
engineering_relevance: Ni–Cr-based coatings, particularly HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC, offer a promising route to improve high-temperature oxidation resistance of SA516 boiler components.
method: Applied Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterized microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports severe oxide spalling and cracking on bare steel, while coated samples developed protective oxides including Cr2O3, TiO2, NiTiO4, and NiO.
watch_item: Results are limited to laboratory air oxidation; long-term durability in actual boiler environments remains to be established.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
